clue.text: Vehicle a flyer used for a tournament once

parts.note: a car is a motor vehicle
the ousel (ouzel) is a bird, the blackbird or ring ouzel

explanation.surface: Someone describes an old-time tournament where a vehicle carried a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: A carousel was a knightly tournament of the seventeenth century, with chariots and pageantry, before the word came to mean a merry-go-round.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the word named a tilting display or knightly contest, an archaic sense now replaced by the fairground ride.

clue.text: Volunteers among sailors at home to be 10

indicators.note: the volunteers are placed among the other letters, so this word signals putting one piece inside the rest

parts.note: ABs are able-bodied seamen, so sailors gives ABS
at home means in
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Reservists mixing with naval men in their quarters decide to stay off drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to another clue: 10 is TEETOTAL, so 'be 10' means stay off alcohol. 'Among' places the volunteers between the sailors and 'at home'.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from drinking alcohol is to choose sobriety, which is what a teetotaller does.

clue.text: First two characters in trouble removed — that's 10 put in a dungeon

indicators.note: the second group of letters is placed inside the first, so put in signals insertion
names which letters go: the opening pair of the word trouble
the opening pair of trouble is taken away, so this word signals a deletion

parts.note: that is, Latin id est, is abbreviated i.e.
10-across is teetotal, abbreviated TT

explanation.surface: Someone in trouble with letters gone is locked up in a cell for being dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is a classic crossword signal for i.e. (id est); 10 refers to TEETOTAL, abbreviated TT. Both go in before the last letter of the shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: An oubliette is a secret pit-like prison reached only through a trapdoor, a kind of underground cell.

clue.text: Novelist found in rear end of carriage

parts.note: the stern is the rear of a ship

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word carriage

explanation.surface: A writer is discovered at the back of a railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was the eighteenth-century author of Tristram Shandy and A Sentimental Journey.

clue.text: An opponent of imperialism — till General Dent agitated!

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up and disturbed, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A general named Dent rages at an anti-imperialist.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of TILL GENERAL DENT uses all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The term was coined for those who wanted Britain to keep to its own shores rather than expand an empire.

clue.text: Vessel carrying everyone for mobilization

indicators.note: the vessel holds the other piece within it, so carrying signals insertion

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A ship takes everyone aboard as the forces are mobilised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A summons to military service is the first step when forces are mobilised.

clue.text: Colour of strong box standing on inverted cask

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece stands on top of the second

parts.note: a chest is a strong box

indicators.note: inverted means turned upside down, so in a down clue the word for cask is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tun is a large cask

explanation.surface: A strong box is placed on top of an upturned barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: TUN turned over gives NUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Chestnut is a reddish-brown shade, named after the nut's shell.

clue.text: Article in Caesar's tongue about a few of the Letts

indicators.note: the result of the first step goes around another letter, so about signals insertion
the article sits inside the language, so in signals insertion

parts.note: Caesar spoke Latin
a is the indefinite article
V is the Roman numeral five, a small number

explanation.surface: A remark on the Roman language mentions a handful of Baltic people.
explanation.walkthrough: A inside LATIN makes LATIAN; that then goes about V.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvian is the adjective for Latvia, home of the Letts, a Baltic people.

clue.text: Plastic covering for article kept in college quarters

indicators.note: the article is held inside the other letters, so kept in signals insertion

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a kind of college
N and E are compass quarters, north and east
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Something to wrap an item stored in a student's rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quarters' suggests lodgings to go with college, but it means compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Polythene film is widely used as a protective wrapping or sheet for goods.

clue.text: American island retreat at one's disposal

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the island's name is read backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: An American's island hideaway is available whenever needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island retreat' suggests a holiday hideaway; it is Elba backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be put to use is available to whoever has it.

clue.text: Like one having duck without ever first touching a drop

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the duck goes around the other letters

parts.note: the teal is a small duck

indicators.note: touching means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side
first picks the opening letter of the word ever

parts.note: a tot is a small drop of spirits

explanation.surface: Someone scoring nothing at cricket never has a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside. 'One' points back to the rest of the clue: someone who never touches a drop. A duck is a score of nothing in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer describes a person who abstains entirely from alcohol, matching one who never takes a drink.

clue.text: Sensible student on desert island

indicators.note: in an across clue, putting one piece on another means placing it after

parts.note: to rat is to desert
Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides
L is for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A level-headed student is stranded on a desert island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like an adjective for the island but is the verb RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasonable, logical person is level-headed and guided by reason.

clue.text: To a large extent the rent is a good husband's concern

indicators.note: most of the following word is kept, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split, a rift

explanation.surface: A tenant's large rent is something a careful husband worries about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid; it is a tear. To husband is to manage resources carefully, the old sense of husbandry.
explanation.definitionFit: Careful economy with money and resources is what good husbandry means.

clue.text: In Verdun it endeavoured to make one

indicators.note: In signals that the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: In the French town of Verdun, someone tried to bring people together.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span verdUN IT Endeavoured.
explanation.definitionFit: To join together into a single whole is to bring things into union.

clue.text: Free a French explorer who has lost weight

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so these words signal a deletion

parts.note: Ernest Shackleton was an Antarctic explorer
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A French adventurer who has slimmed down is set loose.
explanation.walkthrough: SHACKLETON without TON leaves SHACKLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To release from chains or fetters is to set someone at liberty.

clue.text: Favourite uncle somehow concealing a peevish irritability

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hide another letter inside them, so concealing signals insertion
somehow says the letters of uncle are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A favourite uncle hides his ill temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' shuffles UNCLE to ULNCE, which hides A to give ULANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulance is childish sulky bad temper, a sullen touchiness.

clue.text: Duck found in lay-by, sure to be injured

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the letters of the preceding words are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A duck is discovered hurt in a roadside parking place.
explanation.walkthrough: A lay-by is a British roadside parking area.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aylesbury is a white domestic breed of duck named after the Buckinghamshire town.

clue.text: It's made with rare rum

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means strange or odd, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A drink or sugar is produced with some fine rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink; it is the British adjective meaning odd. The whole clue also describes Demerara rum.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara is a Guyanese rum, so the whole clue is a description of the drink itself.

clue.text: Excellent ruler

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means supreme or outstandingly effective, as in a ... remedy

explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign remedy is supremely effective, and a sovereign is a reigning monarch.

clue.text: There's some point in this artist's beard

definitions.text: There's some point in this artist's beard

parts.words: There's some point in this artist's beard
parts.note: names a painter whose portraits made famous a neat pointed beard; point also hints at a lace edging pattern

explanation.surface: A remark that a painter's facial hair has a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: The trim short pointed beard seen in portraits by the Flemish painter is named after him.

clue.text: It's inclined to hang down loosely in Kent

definitions.text: to hang down loosely in Kent
definitions.meaning: a Kentish dialect verb meaning to droop or dangle loosely

explanation.definitionFit: A hillside is a tilted surface, and in Kent dialect the word also meant to sag or dangle.

clue.text: Pretend, as Moriarty presumably did

definitions.meaning: to claim falsely, to make out
Professor Moriarty, Sherlock Holmes's enemy, would have taught as a professor

explanation.definitionFit: To claim something insincerely is to feign it, and a professor teaches or holds a chair.

clue.text: Seagull holding a feast where cattle graze

indicators.note: the gull's name holds the other letters inside, so holding signals insertion

parts.note: the mew is a seagull
a do is a party or feast

explanation.surface: A gull grabs food at a banquet in a field of cows.
explanation.walkthrough: MEW holds A plus DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassy field used for hay or pasture is where livestock feed.

clue.text: Extra accommodation for girl by river?

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
the Exe is a river in Devon, England

explanation.surface: A girl wonders if she should build an extension beside the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an added building or wing that gives more room.

clue.text: Antipathy for county introducing arbitrary rise

indicators.note: the county takes the other letters in, so introducing signals insertion

parts.note: Avon was an English county from 1974 to 1996

indicators.note: arbitrary means random, so the letters of rise appear in no set order

explanation.surface: Resentment towards a county that imposes a random increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arbitrary' scrambles 'rise' to ERSI, which the old county name takes in. Avon was abolished in 1996 but survives in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong dislike or distaste is a feeling of hostility.

clue.text: Crucial to the management that typists should use it

indicators.note: to here joins two pieces so the second follows the first

parts.note: key means crucial
the board is a company's management

explanation.surface: The bosses insist typists must use something vital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crucial to the management' reads as office politics; it is KEY plus BOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Typists press the keys of a typewriter or computer to enter text.

clue.text: Plunged theologian into river? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: into normally puts the first piece inside the second, signalling insertion
reverses the direction of the insertion, so the river goes inside the theologian

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A divine is thrown into a river, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'into' would put the theologian inside the river; 'Quite the opposite' tells you to swap the roles, so the river sits inside the two Ds.
explanation.definitionFit: To douse something is to plunge it into water or drench it.

clue.text: Adviser rejected anger in the latter part of life

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the whole assembly is read in reverse
the anger sits inside the word for old age, so in signals insertion

parts.note: age here means old age
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A counsellor was turned away for losing their temper in old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns the whole assembly round, not just the anger. Egeria was the nymph who advised the Roman king Numa, hence any female counsellor.
explanation.definitionFit: Egeria, the nymph who counselled King Numa, gives her name to any female counsellor or mentor.

clue.text: Soccer violence possibly is? My word!

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in shock about football hooliganism.
explanation.walkthrough: IS MY WORD rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdyism is rough noisy disorderly behaviour, as with football hooligans.
